description: For a final g, use a crisp k sound, not the g in English “go.” After i in the ending -ig, standard German instead uses a soft, hissy sound: raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth and let air pass through.

description: Final “er” usually sounds like a relaxed “uh” (/ɐ/), not the strongly pronounced R in American English “her.” Let your tongue relax instead of curling it back for an R.
